newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK PRIVATE BANKS '96 REAL PROFIT INCREASE 28 PCT.
newsitem.headline: TURK PRIVATE BANKS '96 REAL PROFIT INCREASE 28 PCT.

text.p: Turkish private banks' profits rose 27.7 percent in real terms to 196.1 trillion lira in 1996, from 87.2 trillion lira in 1995, a treasury report said.

"The conditions in 1996 led to the profit increases, but banks may face a profit problem if interest rates on state securities continue to fall or foreign exchange rates go up," the report prepared by the treasury's bank auditors' committee said.
Profits of the four leading private banks -- Is Bankasi, Akbank, Yapi Kredi Bank and Garanti Bankasi -- made up 60.2 percent of the total 1996 profits.
Of the total 69 banks in Turkey, 33 operate as private ones.
Private banks' total balance sheets grew by 25 percent in dollar terms to $43.6 billion in 1996, from $34.9 billion at the end of 1995, the report said.

Their total Turkish lira and foreign currency deposits more than doubled to 3,281 trillion lira, from 1,429 trillion in 1995 and the share of foreign currency deposits in the total fell to 64 percent from 68 percent over the same period.

Main reasons behind the drop in foreign currency deposits were listed as confidence in the financial markets, a move towards realistic foreign exchange policy which reduced speculative expectations in hard currencies, increasing Turkish lira-based investment alternatives and focusing on Turkish lira sources due to rising costs of foreign loans.
Overdue repayments on extended loans of the 33 private banks rose to 7.4 trillion lira in 1996, up 114.4 percent from the previous year.
The average ratio of repurchase agreement (repo) trade volume of the private banks also rose to 23.3 percent of the total deposits in 1996 from 18.4 percent a year ago.
The total repo trade volume made by the 33 private banks stood at 763.2 trillion lira in 1996, up 190 percent from 263.3 trillion lira in 1995.
-- Hatice Aydogdu, Ankara newsroom +90-212-275 08 75 ATA EKS
